assertion_analysis.assertions: held_launch_reservation is None for a parked worker whose supervisor is alive
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Reinstating the base revision's reservation_in_flight (which returns held whenever the recorded supervisor is alive) makes this red; the negative-control log records exactly that failure at base.

assertion_analysis.assertions: reserve_launch_attempt succeeds (returns a reservation) for that same parked run
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Restoring the refusal in reserve_launch_attempt raises CrewError here; independent of the input the test passed in, since the reservation it takes is what is asserted.

assertion_analysis.assertions: a running worker's reservation is still held and names that worker's pid
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Over-widening parked_on_declared_wait to ignore worker liveness returns None here; guards against the over-release direction.
Nothing: held_tick is never set anywhere in the file, so the assertion is true unconditionally.

assertion_analysis.assertions: the sweep resumed the run after the probe turned terminal
assertion_analysis.fails_if: The base revision's resume-refused guard leaves report['resumed'] empty, as the negative-control log shows ('assert wave in {}').

assertion_analysis.assertions: the wake lands within WAKE_BOUND_SECONDS of the probe turning terminal
assertion_analysis.fails_if: A wake that only fired on a later sweep pass would exceed the bound; the two sides are an observation from the sweep report and the test's own sweep cadence, so they do not move together.

findings.summary: `held_tick` is a local Event nothing sets or reads, so the assertion that it is unset cannot fail and the 'tick held for the whole case' claim is unmeasured.
findings.text: non-blocking: `held_tick` is a local threading.Event that no line ever sets or reads, so `assert held_tick.is_set() is False` holds whatever the code does and the case proves nothing about a station tick being held; the done-when's 'station tick held for 30 minutes by an injected delay' clause is therefore unmeasured and the test's own docstring claims it.

findings.summary: Head-arm log header records the base revision plus uncommitted changes while the manifest records the head arm at 2182aea966.
findings.text: non-blocking: the head arm's own header records the base revision 'plus the node's uncommitted worktree changes', while the manifest's after_suite and the fragment record the head arm at 2182aea966; the record names a revision the log does not.

findings.summary: Both gate logs and the manifest's suite records carry an angle-bracket placeholder command instead of the literal command that ran.
findings.text: non-blocking: the header's command line carries the placeholder '<19 related test files plus the node's new test file>' instead of the literal file list, and the manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite commands carry '<tree>' and '<19 related test files>' the same way, so neither arm can be re-run from the record although the done-when requires a literal command in every log.

findings.summary: A just-resumed attempt reads as parked until its supervisor writes the new worker record, reporting the reservation it just took as free.
findings.text: non-blocking: the parked reading is taken from the run's worker record, which the supervisor rewrites only once the resumed worker is spawned, so in the window between a resume being admitted and its worker.json landing a run that is genuinely running still reads as parked and its reservation reads as free.

findings.summary: Comments narrate the incident that motivated the change instead of the mechanism.
findings.text: non-blocking: the comment explains the change by its incident ('which is what left one run forty minutes past the end of its job') rather than by the mechanism, which the repository's comment rules forbid.
